subject.title: San Diego County — Measure B (Measure to Fund San Diego County Health & Safety Services)

strong: MEASURE TO FUND SAN DIEGO COUNTY HEALTH & SAFETY SERVICES

text: To clean-up sewage pollution in Tijuana River Valley, improve wildfire prevention, emergency response, access to healthcare, food assistance, childhood development services, and authorized administrative expenses; shall the measure authorizing a half-cent sales tax raising an estimated $400,000,000 to $450,000,000 annually, requiring citizen oversight, public spending disclosure, and independent annual audits, and lasting until ended by voters, be adopted?
This measure requires Simple Majority (50%+1) of those voting on the measure.

strong: MEASURE TO FUND SAN DIEGO COUNTY HEALTH & SAFETY
SERVICES

text: This measure was placed on the ballot by a petition signed by the requisite number of voters.

This measure, if approved by a majority vote of qualified electors, would impose a transaction and use tax of a half cent per dollar on the sale of all tangible personal property in the County of San Diego, in both incorporated and unincorporated areas. The tax would be administered similarly to collection of other state and local sales taxes.

The tax is subject to certain specified exemptions and exclusions that are generally consistent with state and locally imposed sales taxes. The sales tax would remain in effect until repealed by voters. It is estimated that the sales tax would generate approximately $400,000,000 to $450,000,000 per year.

This measure would establish a Protect San Diego County’s Health and Safety Fund for revenues generated. Funds would only be used for specified purposes, including efforts to stop sewage pollution in the Tijuana River Valley, wildfire prevention and emergency response, access to healthcare, food assistance, and childhood development services, and authorized administrative expenses. The measure would allocate funding as follows:
Stopping sewage pollution in the Tijuana River Valley: 22.5%
Public safety services and wildfire prevention: 17.5%
Healthcare, childcare, and nutrition services: 60%

The measure would establish a twelve-member oversight committee, which would audit how funds are spent to ensure compliance with the measure’s requirements. The Board of Supervisors for the County of San Diego would appoint eleven of the twelve members of this committee, who would be required to have certain qualifications specified in the measure. The twelfth member of this committee would be the County of San Diego Auditor. The measure would also prohibit the use of funds for such things as elected official or County employee salaries, lobbyist contracts, or government office renovations. The measure would require public disclosure of all spending.
A YES vote would impose a half-cent sales tax for use to clean-up sewage pollution in the Tijuana River Valley, public safety, wildfire prevention, healthcare, childcare and nutrition services.
A NO vote would reject a half-cent sales tax for use to clean-up sewage pollution in the Tijuana River Valley, public safety, wildfire prevention, healthcare, childcare and nutrition services.

text: Measure B fights the worsening Tijuana River sewage crisis closing beaches, making kids sick and poisoning our air and water. Instead of cutting clean-water protections, Measure B upgrades water safety infrastructure and funds emergency health response for South County families.

strong: YES ON B: HOLD POLITICIANS ACCOUNTABLE.

text: We’ve carefully analyzed Measure B and strongly urge you to VOTE NO! It will cost you and all County taxpayers more money with too much uncertainty and unclear oversight.
In a time of rising gas and food prices, Measure B will raise the average San Diego household’s taxes by

strong: hundreds of dollars

text: every year.
Measure B contains

strong: no sunset clause

text: that allows voters to reauthorize it based on how well politicians spend the new money. If approved,

strong: we will pay the new tax forever

text: unless voters gather signatures to repeal it.

Measure B creates a supposed citizens’ oversight committee that seems designed to specifically exclude any taxpayer advocacy representatives. However, direct recipients of the new taxes are given spots on this committee to oversee money they receive themselves! This is a

strong: huge conflict of interest!

text: Measure B contains

strong: no year-over-year performance targets

text: that would allow citizens to measure and track results.
Measure B adds a permanent new revenue stream onto a fiscal structure the Taxpayers Association has already identified as

strong: unsustainable

text: on its current path.
Local media reports that County officials

strong: refuse to say

text: whether Measure B would reopen one or more County labor contracts to increase employee salaries & benefits, creating

strong: uncertainty for
voters

text: in how the money will truly be spent.
It doesn’t add up.

strong: VOTE NO on Measure B!
